web_title: 8. Stage 2 Technical Structure, Institutional Flow & Momentum Setup
book_title: Chapter 8: Reading the Tape — Trend, Volume & Momentum Opportunity
question: Does the weekly and daily price structure confirm institutional accumulation in Stage 2, and does Friday's pullback offer an actionable, low-extension entry?

epigraph.quote: Never buy a stock because it is cheap on a spreadsheet while its thirty-week moving average is rolling over; buy quality only when the tape confirms institutions are quietly absorbing supply.
epigraph.author: Stan Weinstein Tape Discipline

web_blocks.html: Manorama Industries trades in a confirmed Stan Weinstein Stage 2 uptrend as of November 13, 2026 [27]. At ₹1,984.10, the stock sits 16.30% above its rising 30-week SMA (₹1,706.09) and 24.12% above its 200-day SMA (₹1,598.49) [27]. It has gained 50.31% over the past year and 46.42% over six months [27]. Crucially, the stock is not extended: it trades just +4.54% above its 10-week EMA (₹1,898.01) and +3.00% above its 50-day SMA (₹1,926.38) [27].

Friday’s session (November 13, 2026) warrants caution before deploying fresh cash. MANORAMA fell -5.52% to ₹1,984.10 on 460,318 shares—2.83x its 30-day average volume (3.58x its 20-day average) [27]. Over the past 25 sessions, the stock has logged 6 distribution days with -6.62% 28-day relative strength, even while remaining up +5.25% on the week [27]. Weekly RSI(14) holds at 60.88 and daily RSI(14) reset to 55.53 as price landed near the 20D EMA (₹1,928.65) and 50D SMA (₹1,926.38) [27, 31].

web_blocks.takeaway: MANORAMA sits right at the upper lip of its ₹1,869.54–₹1,957.58 support buy zone with +4.54% 10W EMA extension and a clear invalidation floor below the 30W/40W moving averages at ₹1,664.

web_blocks.html: Shareholding disclosures confirm institutional accumulation behind the move. Between June and September 2026, Domestic Institutional Investors more than doubled their stake from 2.63% to 6.40% [1, 30]. Foreign Institutional Investors also lifted their holding from 3.22% to 4.16% [1, 30]. The -2.94% dip in promoter stake (from 54.32% to 51.38%) reflects June 2026 QIP dilution, not promoter selling [1, 30].

On the 4-hour chart, RSI sits at 55.04 near the 20-period EMA (₹1,961.20) and 50-period SMA (₹1,894.75) [31]. Because intraday_4h_turn is not yet triggered and 25-day distribution sits at 6 days, we do not buy Friday’s close immediately [31]. Instead, we wait for price to stabilize inside the ₹1,870–₹1,960 support zone on drying volume before deploying new capital [27]. Manorama is not in the NSE F&O segment (NOT_OPTIONABLE_OR_ILLIQUID), so all exposure uses cash equity [31].

web_blocks.title: No-FOMO Tape Rule: Respecting the ₹1,664 Structural Stop
paragraphs: With a 14-day ATR of ₹84.14 (~4.2% of price), Manorama is a high-beta (1.39) mid-cap that routinely swings 5–8% around earnings [27]. Setting a tight 5% stop invites whipsaw; placing the structural invalidation stop at ₹1,664.02 (just beneath the 40-week EMA at ₹1,679.21 and 30-week SMA at ₹1,706.09) gives the Stage 2 trend room to breathe while capping per-share risk at ~16.1% from CMP and ~15.1% from ₹1,960 [27].

book_paragraphs: Having tested the business blind and priced its future in Chapter 7, you and I now turn to the tape. Why does a fundamental investor care about moving averages? Because even the finest specialty-fats business in India can bleed your capital for eighteen months if you buy it right as institutions are quietly distributing shares into a Stage 3 top. Conversely, when a compounder is in a healthy Stage 2 uptrend and pulls back into institutional support on a reset RSI, the market is telling you that big balance sheets are still absorbing supply.

As of Friday, November 13, 2026, Manorama Industries is squarely in Stan Weinstein's Stage 2. At ₹1,984.10, the stock is up 50.31% over the past year and sits 16.30% above its rising 30-week simple moving average of ₹1,706.09, and 24.12% above its 200-day moving average of ₹1,598.49. Just as important, it is not stretched: it trades only 4.54% above its 10-week EMA of ₹1,898.01 and 3.00% above its 50-day SMA of ₹1,926.38.

Now let's look closely at Friday's session, because that -5.52% red candle on 2.83 times average volume (460,318 shares versus a 30-day average of 162,430) is the exact kind of bar that scares retail investors out of great setups. Zoom out to the weekly timeframe: the stock is still up 5.25% for the week, weekly RSI sits at a constructive 60.88, and daily RSI cooled right back to 55.53. That is a textbook post-earnings shakeout pulling back toward the 20-day EMA (₹1,928.65) and 50-day SMA (₹1,926.38), not a Stage 4 breakdown.

Look under the hood at the shareholding pattern to confirm who is on the other side of these swings. Between June and September 2026, Domestic Institutional Investors more than doubled their stake from 2.63% to 6.40%, and Foreign Institutional Investors stepped up from 3.22% to 4.16%. What Screener's automated screen flagged as a 2.94% drop in promoter holding—from 54.32% to 51.38%—was simply the arithmetic dilution of issuing new shares in the ₹500 crore June 2026 QIP, not promoters dumping stock.

book_subsections.title: Why Cash Equity Only—And Where the Floor Sits
paragraphs: If you were hoping to structure a call spread or LEAPS overlay, our options check confirms Manorama is not in the NSE F&O segment. There is no liquid listed options chain here, which means you and I express this view strictly through cash equity sizing.

And because Manorama carries a 1.39 beta and an ₹84.14 average true range—meaning a 4% daily move is normal weather—you cannot place a tight stop-loss right under yesterday's low. Instead, we anchor our structural invalidation stop at ₹1,664, just beneath the 40-week EMA (₹1,679.21) and 30-week SMA (₹1,706.09). As long as the stock holds above that weekly floor, the Stage 2 institutional uptrend remains intact.

callouts.title: NARRATOR'S REFLECTION
callouts.text: Good entries feel slightly uncomfortable. When a Stage 2 leader drops 5.5% on heavy volume right into its 20-day and 50-day moving averages while weekly structure stays green, patience to buy in two tranches—one near CMP and one in the ₹1,870–₹1,960 shelf—beats chasing breakouts at 52-week highs.

book_subsections.title: Reading Institutional Footprints in the Volume & Shareholding Tape
paragraphs: One of the biggest mistakes retail traders make is treating every -5% red candle as a reason to panic. Look at the context around November 13, 2026: Manorama had rallied 46.4% over six months, briefly touching ₹2,161, and then pulled back -5.52% to ₹1,984.10 on 2.83 times its 30-day average volume. If the stock had broken below its 30-week moving average (₹1,706.09) on that volume, we would call it distribution and step aside. Instead, it landed right on top of its 20-day EMA (₹1,928.65) and 50-day SMA (₹1,926.38), leaving the stock up +5.25% for the week with weekly RSI at 60.88.

Pair that chart with the September 2026 shareholding disclosure: DIIs more than doubled their stake from 2.63% to 6.40% and FIIs rose to 4.16% through the QIP. Big domestic mutual funds do not underwrite a ₹500 crore placement in June only to abandon the stock at the 50-day moving average in November. As long as ₹1,664 holds on a weekly closing basis, the Stage 2 institutional accumulation trend remains our ally.

book_subsections.title: Comparing Weekly, Daily, and 4-Hour Support Shelves
paragraphs: Let's zoom in on the exact price shelves across all three timeframes so you know what a healthy pullback looks like versus a broken trend. On the weekly chart, the primary trend anchor is the 10-week EMA at ₹1,898.01 and the 30-week SMA at ₹1,706.09, with weekly RSI at 60.88. On the daily chart, the 20-day EMA (₹1,928.65) and 50-day SMA (₹1,926.38) sit almost on top of each other—creating a tight institutional demand band inside our ₹1,870–₹1,960 buy zone.

Even on the 4-hour chart, RSI cooled to 55.04 right near the 20-period 4H EMA (₹1,961.20) and 50-period 4H SMA (₹1,894.75). That multi-timeframe alignment—where weekly, daily, and 4-hour moving averages all converge between ₹1,870 and ₹1,960—gives us high confidence in both our entry shelf and our ₹1,664 invalidation floor.
